step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Analyze Visual Components: Identify nodes drawn on the whiteboard: Route 53, WAF, CloudFront, EC2 (Pass Secure Load Balancer), EKS, Elasticsearch (mapped to canonical AWS service OpenSearch), ElastiCache, S3, Aurora, EC2 (NFS Server), VPN, Lambda, Redshift, and EC2 (Mail Server).
2. Identify Visual Edges: Trace arrows starting from Route 53 -> WAF -> CloudFront. From CloudFront, arrows point to S3 (static assets) and EC2 (LB). From EC2 (LB), an arrow points to EKS. From EKS, arrows point to OpenSearch, ElastiCache, EC2 (NFS), Aurora, and S3. Bottom components (VPN, Lambda, RedShift, EC2 Mail) are standalone without drawn arrows.
3. Sequence: Construct logical sequence `flow_id: 0` representing incoming web traffic processing and backend service interaction.

edges.notes: DNS query and user requests pass through Route 53 to WAF
Protected web traffic sent to CloudFront CDN
CloudFront behavior routes requests for static images directly to S3
CloudFront routes dynamic traffic to Pass Secure load balancer on EC2
Load balancer forwards web requests to EKS container applications
EKS queries Elasticsearch for catalog indexing and search
EKS queries ElastiCache for user navigation sessions and application cache
EKS mounts and accesses shared files from EC2 NFS server
EKS performs database transactions against Aurora MySQL
EKS stores generated static elements and log data to S3
